title: The decisions behind it
subtitle: Four choices that shaped the architecture - and what each one bought me.

items.title: UI-first instead of schema-first
items.description: Traditional CMSes force the design to fit the data model. Here the model absorbs whatever the design needs, so a new section is a key and a JSON fallback - not a migration, a resolver and an admin form.

items.title: Fallbacks that keep the site alive
items.description: Every section ships with a JSON fallback compiled into the bundle. If the backend or database is unreachable, pages still render fully - the CMS degrades to a static site instead of a 500.

items.title: One entity instead of N models
items.description: Multiple live sections across three pages share a single table. Adding a fourth page costs no backend work at all - the content engine already handles it.

items.title: Tested where it actually breaks
items.description: Unit tests cover content and media services including MinIO rollback paths; Playwright drives the real admin panel through create, edit, delete, reorder and upload against a live database.
